questions.question: When driving a bobtail tractor, what should you know?

options.text: Bobtails cannot drive as fast as tractors with trailers.
Bobtails are harder to stop than tractors with trailers.
Bobtails are illegal in most states.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bobtails are harder to stop than tractors with trailers.
questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor has no trailer attached. It takes longer to stop a bobtail than it takes to stop a tractor pulling a loaded trailer.

questions.question: When traveling slower than 40 mph, how many seconds of space should you leave for every 10 feet of vehicle length?
questions.correctAnswerText: One second
questions.explanation: At speeds below 40 mph, leave at least one second of space for every 10 feet of your vehicle's length. At higher speeds, add one more second.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks?

options.text: Get out and call for help.
Keep trying to remove the vehicle from the tracks.
Walk down the tracks to look for a train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out and call for help.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, exit immediately and walk away from the tracks. Call emergency services for help.

questions.question: When checking the engine compartment, what should you do?

options.text: The parking brake should not be engaged.
Put the gearshift in first gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block the wheels.
questions.explanation: Before checking the engine, set the parking brake and block the wheels. Check the engine before starting it.

questions.question: Who must provide emergency response information?
questions.correctAnswerText: The shipper
questions.explanation: The shipper of hazardous materials must provide emergency response information to the driver.

questions.question: A driver should always:
questions.correctAnswerText: Have an emergency plan.
questions.explanation: While driving, look ahead for hazards. Plan what you would do if each hazard becomes dangerous.

questions.question: Why are roads slippery when it first rains?

options.text: Rain mixes with oil on the road.
The water has nowhere to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rain mixes with oil on the road.
questions.explanation: When it first rains, water mixes with oil and grease on the road. This creates a slippery film. As rain continues, this film washes away.

questions.question: During an inspection, brake pads should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Free of oil or grease.
questions.explanation: Brake pads and shoes must not have oil, grease, or brake fluid on them.

questions.question: If a federal inspector finds your vehicle unsafe, what can they do?

options.text: Take you to a garage to fix your vehicle.
Ask you to fix your vehicle's problems.
Take the vehicle out of service until it is fixed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take the vehicle out of service until it is fixed.
questions.explanation: If a federal or state inspector decides a vehicle is unsafe, they can remove it from service until it is repaired.

questions.question: Tank vehicles usually have:
questions.correctAnswerText: High centers of gravity.
questions.explanation: Tank vehicles have high centers of gravity. Drive carefully, especially when turning or taking curves.

questions.question: When doing pre-trip inspections, what should you do?

options.text: Do the inspections the same way each time.
It is fine to check items in a different order each time.
You do not need to inspect every item each time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do the inspections the same way each time.
questions.explanation: Always do pre-trip inspections the same way. This helps you remember all the important steps and makes it less likely you will forget to check something.

questions.question: What must a person supervising tank loading do?

options.text: They do not need to be able to move the vehicle.
They must be a licensed firefighter.
They do not need to know about the materials being loaded.
They must stay within 25 feet of the tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: They must stay within 25 feet of the tank.
questions.explanation: A qualified person must watch tank loading and unloading. They must stay alert and within 25 feet of the tank. They must see the tank clearly, know the hazards of the materials, know emergency procedures, and be able to move the tank if needed.

questions.question: During a trip, which shut-off valves should be open?

options.text: All shut-off valves should be open.
The rear shut-off valves should be open.
All shut-off valves should be open, except the rear shut-off valves.
No shut-off valves should be open.

questions.correctAnswerText: All shut-off valves should be open, except the rear shut-off valves.
questions.explanation: When starting a trip, open all shut-off valves except the last ones on the rear trailer. This makes sure air reaches the brakes on all trailers and does not escape from the back of the vehicle.

questions.question: If you are transporting explosives, where may you leave your vehicle unattended?
questions.correctAnswerText: In a safe haven.
questions.explanation: When transporting hazardous materials, you may only leave your vehicle unattended in a safe haven. A safe haven is an approved location for parking vehicles loaded with explosives.

questions.question: When checking your mirrors while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use the passenger side mirror.
Do not use the driver's side mirror.
Look in each mirror for a long time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both mirrors.
questions.explanation: To drive safely, you need to know what is happening on all sides of your vehicle. Check all mirrors often while driving.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good way to reduce crashes when turning right?

options.text: Keep the rear of the vehicle close to the curb.
Leave space open on your right side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave space open on your right side.
questions.explanation: When turning right, do not turn too wide to the left. Keep the rear of your vehicle close to the curb. Leaving space on your right side while turning right may make other drivers think you are turning left, and they may try to pass you on the right.

questions.question: What should you know about joggers wearing headsets?

options.text: They are usually aware of what is happening around them.
They may not be aware of what is happening around them.
They can clearly hear traffic sounds.
They usually do not have music playing.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may not be aware of what is happening around them.
questions.explanation: Be careful around pedestrians, joggers, and cyclists wearing headphones. They may not hear traffic clearly and may not know you are there.

questions.question: What determines your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
questions.correctAnswerText: How much you drink
questions.explanation: Your BAC depends on how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Only time can lower your BAC as your body processes the alcohol naturally.

questions.question: What should you do to make night driving easier?

options.text: Dim the instrument panel lights as much as possible while still reading the gauges.
Do not take a nap before driving.
Use only your low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dim the instrument panel lights as much as possible while still reading the gauges.
questions.explanation: Bright interior lights make it hard to see outside at night. Turn off the interior light and set the instrument lights to the lowest level that lets you read the gauges easily.

questions.question: If your coolant level is low, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Add more coolant.
questions.explanation: Check the oil level, coolant level, and windshield washer fluid when you inspect the engine. Your engine needs enough coolant in both cold and hot weather.
